paper.title: Cerulean Protein Tagging Enhances Immunogenicity and Osimertinib Response of Transplantable Murine EGFR Mutant Lung Cancer Cell Lines.
paper.abstract: Lung cancers bearing mutations in epidermal growth factor receptors (EGFR) exhibit marked, but incomplete responses to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) like osimertinib. We previously developed genetically-engineered mouse models (GEMMs) for EGFR exon 19 deletion (del19) and L860R (mouse equivalent of L858R). Sequences encoding mC3 cerulean fluorescent protein were included to mark emergent tumor cells. Orthotopic implantation of mEGFRdel19 cell lines into syngeneic C57BL/6J mice yielded tumors that were eliminated upon osimertinib therapy which is not typically observed in patients while mEGFR-L860R cell lines failed to establish tumors. Herein, mEGFRdel19 and mEGFR-L860R cell lines formed tumors in non-induced mEGFRdel19 and mEGFR-L860R GEMMs and green fluorescent protein-transgenic mice, supporting mC3-derived epitopes as mediators of immunoelimination. CRISPR-Cas9 mediated disruption of the mC3 cerulean sequence in established mEGFR cell lines yielded two independent mC3-deleted cell lines that formed orthotopic tumors and exhibited partial osimertinib responses. These studies provide a cautionary tale regarding use of fluorescent proteins in murine cancer models and reinforce host immunity as a participant in anti-tumor TKI responses initiated. These mC3-deleted cell lines serve as improved models to explore mechanisms of incomplete TKI response, acquired resistance and cancer cell interaction with the host immune microenvironment.

summary.text: In a cell-line study, CRISPR-Cas9 disruption of the mC3 cerulean sequence in established mEGFR cell lines generated two independent mC3-deleted lines that formed orthotopic tumors. These cell lines exhibited partial responses to osimertinib, a finding relevant to EGFR exon 19 deletion and L860R variants in the context of host immunity.
